problem: The TODO handoff procedure names two machine verifications, todo_compaction.py and todo_handoff.py, but there is no single machine command that runs both, and nothing detects that only one was run. On 2026-08-07 a TODO edit passed todo_handoff.py while violating todo_compaction.py's single-active-ID rule, was committed, and survived two further commits until an unrelated full test run exposed it. A second manual weakness amplified the miss: the executor's commit chain piped the test run into tail, so the failing exit code was masked and the commit condition 'tests pass' was judged by eye instead of by the machine. Both weaknesses are instances of the recorded lesson that a declared rule without a machine check does not hold.
impact: a TODO revision violating a machine rule was treated as verified and committed three times
the commit condition requiring passing tests was bypassed unnoticed because the exit code was masked by a pipe
the two-step verification depends on the executor remembering both steps, which is exactly the manual-rework class the development policy routes to machine candidates
boundary: preserve this observation as immutable source
do not treat this observation as an Improvement Candidate, Human Triage Decision or Issue Record
do not modify todo_handoff.py, todo_compaction.py, the procedure document or any test on the basis of this observation alone
the remedy must not introduce hooks or guarded commits
